issues.description: The problem statement and the template define a public method named singFarmSong() to play the farm song for all animals, but the solution implementation introduces a method named playFarmSong() instead of singFarmSong(). This name/signature mismatch means students following the solution would not find the expected singFarmSong() implementation (and any tests or the provided Main that call singFarmSong() would fail to compile or run against the solution).
issues.suggestedFix: Ensure the solution uses the same public method name and signature as the problem/template: implement public void singFarmSong() (or add a public singFarmSong() that delegates to playFarmSong()). Rename playFarmSong() to singFarmSong() or provide a singFarmSong() wrapper to preserve compatibility with the specification and tests.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template define and refer to a public Farm method named singFarmSong(), but the solution implementation provides a public method named playFarmSong() instead. This inconsistent method name for the same conceptual operation (play/sing the farm song) breaks the direct mapping between the exercise specification and the solution/template, likely confusing students about which method to implement or call.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the solution's public method playFarmSong() to singFarmSong(), or add a public singFarmSong() that delegates to the existing playFarmSong() implementation so the method name matches the problem statement and template.
